data.revised_prompt: The X-shaped geometric layout of four red dots connected by two intersecting blue diagonal lines in <Picture 1> is <Subject 1>. The solid black background in <Picture 1> is <Subject 2>. The target image shows a photorealistic 8K industrial design rendering of a cold-grey quadcopter seen from a direct overhead view, positioned according to the exact spatial geometry of <Subject 1> against <Subject 2>, with the original red dots and blue lines replaced by physical aircraft components. <Subject 1> supplies the exact motor hub positions, spacing, arm trajectories, and framing transferred to the new quadcopter. <Subject 2> is fully preserved. The quadcopter features a streamlined central fuselage with a 60-degree edge angle, crafted from matte carbon fiber and finished in a cold grey color scheme, with a discreetly integrated GPS antenna on its top surface. Four foldable arms extend outward along the exact paths of the former blue lines of <Subject 1>, utilizing modular quick-release connectors at their joints and featuring an 80-centimeter wing curvature radius profile. Each arm terminates precisely at the four corner coordinates of <Subject 1> in place of the removed red dots, where reinforced motor covers house the four motor hubs. Translucent ABS propellers with a subtle nano-coating sheen are mounted over each hub, angled at 52 degrees relative to the frame. Anodized aluminum honeycomb grilles are recessed into the fuselage panels, accented by a glowing blue LED light band tracing the structural edges. Soft 5500K overhead lighting illuminates the craft from directly above, casting crisp, high-contrast shadows across the carbon fiber weave, chamfered edges, and rotor blades while maintaining the exact scale and centered framing of <Subject 1>.
